chunks.text: ILKIN ISLER, Ph.D. ilkinisler@gmail.com LinkedIn Google Scholar ilkinisler.com

Senior AI Engineer working in a forward-deployed role: meets with business teams, scopes complex business needs, and builds the AI solution from first prototype to trusted production. Builds models, not just uses them: Ph.D. in Computer Science focused on designing novel neural network architectures, with hands-on work across computer vision, NLP, agentic systems, automation, and dataset creation.

Works across the full LLM stack: architecture fundamentals, pre-training and fine-tuning, evaluation, serving and inference, RAG over vector databases, inference optimization for speed and cost, and securing LLM applications. Independently built MCPGates, the organization's enterprise AI platform (20+ production applications), and its first RAG and evaluation systems; leads a five-person team across AI infrastructure, Finance, and Estimating & Budgeting.
LLM Foundations: Transformer architecture (tokenization, attention, sampling), prompt engineering, LLM serving and inference, inference optimization (latency and cost), LLM security
Retrieval & Knowledge Graphs: RAG (vector, hybrid BM25 + vector, and GraphRAG), temporal knowledge graphs (Graphiti-style, built from scratch), data and document ingestion
Agents: Multi-agent systems, agent orchestration, MCP servers, function calling, agent skills, human-in-the-loop systems

Evaluation & Trustworthy AI: Hallucination detection, groundedness evaluation, citation verification, Vectara HHEM, LLM-as-judge, RAGAS, DeepEval, MRR, benchmark and synthetic data creation, regression analysis, uncertainty quantification, explainable AI

Machine Learning & Deep Learning: PyTorch, MONAI; vision transformers (Swin UNETR), CNNs (U-Net), GANs, LSTMs, gradient boosting (XGBoost); multi-GPU distributed training (DDP), neural network architecture design, pre-training and fine-tuning (self-supervised, contrastive, transfer learning), medical image segmentation
Languages, Data & Tools: Python (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, spaCy), SQL, FastAPI, LlamaIndex, pgvector (Postgres), Neo4j, SQLite
UNIVERSAL CREATIVE Orlando, FL
Senior AI Engineer, AI Strategy & Solutions Aug 2025 - Present
Independently architected, built, and deployed MCPGates, the in-house enterprise AI platform that hosts the team's 20+ production AI applications in one place.

New applications ship faster because they reuse shared core components (retrieval and reinforcement learning pipelines, service-account connections to external data sources, MCP servers, tool calling, and agent skills) and inherit one Microsoft Entra ID single sign-on (SSO), role-based access control (RBAC), and a cybersecurity-approved architecture instead of repeating security approval for each one. Serves 200-300 users across multiple business units, with Application Insights monitoring and logging dashboards.

Lead the Finance AI initiative as solution architect and responsible owner: designed from scratch three human-in-the-loop applications for reporting and forecasting to replace a frequently reworked, file-per-project spreadsheet process, and lead the developers building them.

Cash Flow & Earned Value is in production with 70+ finance users globally, unifying finance data in one place and saving users 15-30 minutes per analysis and about an hour per forecast; Monthly Update Insights (top cost drivers each month) and Risk & Contingency (transaction risk flags) have their first versions in production, with more capabilities in development.

Independently architected, built, and deployed Universal Creative's first LLM and RAG evaluation pipelines, scoring hallucination, groundedness, citation correctness, and factual consistency. They gate new methods before production, monitor live chatbots with hallucination scores, and select the best grounded answer at runtime (or decline to answer when none is grounded) across four production applications, including Specs Q&A and Pricing Intelligence.

Lead the Estimating & Budgeting AI initiative as solution architect and responsible owner: designed from scratch the Estimator Builder, an end-to-end, human-in-the-loop suite of 12 purpose-built AI applications for ~80 users, and lead the developers building it, with 6+ shipped.

It includes Drawing Intelligence (reads design drawings and generates scope), Concept Estimate Automation (converts messy, non-standardized show element lists into structured estimates and tracks how they change), and Pricing Intelligence (retrieves everything previously paid for any item from more than 2 million files). Cut estimating from days to minutes and made it traceable and consistent.

Independently architected, built, and deployed a project-intelligence application that shows senior leadership what changed across a project and how it affects budgets, plans, and schedules. Built on a temporal knowledge graph (similar to Graphiti, using Neo4j): project decks and updates from design, scheduling, estimating, budgeting, and finance systems are ingested as episodes, LLMs extract entities and relationships into a graph that keeps every fact's history, and hybrid semantic, keyword, and graph-traversal retrieval answers questions about them.

Co-developed the data ingestion pipeline that made unstructured files plus structured data searchable across the organization and its contractors, from invoices, RFIs, change orders, and issues to PRDs, meeting notes, presentations, emails, and screenshots, powering retrieval for MCPGates applications.

Lead the five-person AI engineering team as technical lead across the infrastructure, finance, and cost-estimating workstreams, delivering on scope, schedule, and budget; co-authored the AI engineering guidance (build and deployment, retrieval, hallucination detection, evaluation, data security) that external vendors must meet, ran two AI lunch-and-learns (~100 attendees), and advised senior leaders on AI adoption in 5-6 working sessions.
AI Software Engineer, Engineering & Safety Jan 2025 - Aug 2025

Independently architected, built, and deployed the company's first retrieval-enabled chatbot for Engineering & Safety over engineering specifications, with RAG, hallucination detection, groundedness scoring, citation verification, topic modeling, metadata tagging, and structured extraction. Evaluated each component on self-built benchmark datasets, including synthetic question-answer data, using MRR for retrieval and RAGAS, DeepEval, BERTScore, ROUGE, and LLM-as-judge for factual consistency and response quality. This work became the core of MCPGates and its production evaluation pipelines.
NORTHWESTERN UNIVERSITY, DEPARTMENT OF RADIOLOGY Chicago, IL
Doctoral Researcher, Machine and Hybrid Intelligence Lab May 2023 - Dec 2024

Led collaborations across multidisciplinary teams to improve medical image visualization tools with detection and segmentation capabilities for oncology and move AI models closer to real-world clinical deployment.

Managed project timelines and deliverables, and wrote the technical documentation supporting AI model development and interpretation for clinical use. UNIVERSITY OF CENTRAL FLORIDA, COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING AND COMPUTER SCIENCE Orlando, FL
Graduate Teaching Assistant Aug 2023 - Dec 2024
Assisted with Advanced Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Computer Networks courses, and taught ~4 lectures.
Graduate Research Assistant Jan 2021 - Aug 2023

Designed novel 3D neural network architectures and compound loss functions combining overlap and boundary-distance objectives for tumor and organ-at-risk segmentation, trained with multi-GPU distributed training (PyTorch DDP) on ~1,000 3D CT and MRI volumes merged and harmonized from multiple datasets, expanded with extensive data augmentation; self-supervised and uncertainty-guided coarse-to-fine approaches achieved state-of-the-art results at publication (IEEE ICECCME 2023, IEEE ACDSA 2025), including raising the transformer-based Swin UNETR's Dice from 0.47 to 0.64, and an improved U-Net reached ~80% vs. 63% Dice over baseline (SPIE Medical Imaging 2022).
Predicted cancer patient survival from radiomics and hand-crafted imaging features.

Developed uncertainty quantification, explainability, and anatomy-aware post-processing methods that guided the model to refine its uncertain regions, improving accuracy, and gave clinicians uncertainty estimates showing when to rely on its output; validated reliability with a broad set of segmentation metrics, including Dice and HD95, alongside confidence and failure analysis.
Co-authored a multi-institutional, five-center pancreas segmentation study (767 MRI scans from 499 participants, plus CT from 1,350 patients) published in Medical Image Analysis.
Python Developer (Contract), Universal Orlando Resort (Orlando, 2022): resolved 100+ vulnerabilities in cloud data pipelines and optimized ML workflows with Azure Databricks and MLflow.
Data Analyst, Simsoft Information Technologies (Ankara, 2020): built LSTM models for anomaly detection and predictive maintenance on industrial sensor data; modeled COVID-19 spread.
Research Intern, UCF Synthetic Reality Lab (Orlando, 2019): applied GANs to facial expression recognition and human-to-avatar translation.
Data Analyst Intern, Carbon Health (San Francisco, 2018): built predictive models that cut clinic wait times by 30%.

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.text: The Mind to Move Mountains

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.text: Ilkin Isler '22MS '25PhD left the familiarity of home in Turkey to study AI at UCF - a daring choice that resulted in research improving the assessment of cancerous tumors and supporting better patient care.

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.text: Nothing motivates Ilkin Isler '22MS '25PhD quite like this phrase: “It can't be done.”

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.text: When Isler says candidly, “Working on my Ph.D. is the most difficult thing I've ever faced,” there's a montage of difficult things in her life to consider - physical and mental, past and present.

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.text: For example, in August 2025, the recent computer science doctoral graduate began work as a senior artificial intelligence (AI) engineer at Universal Creative. Her role involved analyzing complex white papers and developing state-of-the-art AI systems from scratch - all for the purpose of improving the safety of park guests.

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.text: “I find solutions for high-risk applications,” Isler says, “which is a good description for what I love to do.”

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.text: “… when I hear something can't be done, it motivates me to make it happen.” - Ilkin Isler '22MS '25PhD

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.text: The fact that her work requires fortitude also fits Isler well. In high school in Turkey, she once walked into a gym “just for something to do.” A trainer immediately suggested she head to the cardio area, where she'd blend in easily. Isler, however, saw the powerlifting space and thought, “ That's what I want to do.”

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.text: “I had to teach myself how to do [powerlifting],” she says. “People probably thought I'd give up, but when I hear something can't be done, it motivates me to make it happen.”

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.text: Self-taught and competing despite her small frame, Isler went on to become a European powerlifting champion.

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.text: All of this is important for understanding the person who, while studying at UCF, helped develop an AI model to assess cancerous tumors.

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.section: Using Computer Imaging to Enhance Patient Care
chunks.text: Guided by a team of advisors, Isler came up with a way to feed medical imaging into an algorithm that measures shapes and textures with more speed, precision and consistency than is currently possible. Given such accurate information, an oncologist could make quicker, more confident decisions - improving overall patient care.

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.section: Using Computer Imaging to Enhance Patient Care
chunks.text: “… [Ilkin's] work helps push the field forward in an important and timely way.” - David Mohaisen, UCF computer science professor

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.section: Using Computer Imaging to Enhance Patient Care
chunks.text: “The problem she chose to work on is inherently difficult for several reasons,” says David Mohaisen, UCF computer science professor and one of her advisors. “Medical imaging is a high-stakes domain where errors have serious clinical consequences.”

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.section: Using Computer Imaging to Enhance Patient Care
chunks.text: “It's also a mature and crowded research area, with competitive works focusing on incremental benchmark gains rather than addressing deeper issues, such as reliability, uncertainty and clinical integration,” Mohaisen continues. “Instead of chasing marginal improvements, Ilkin focused on meaningful outcomes. Her work helps push the field forward in an important and timely way.”

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.section: Using Computer Imaging to Enhance Patient Care
chunks.text: Yet the breakthrough alone, and the work that went into it, does not fully capture what Isler faced at the dizzying start of her doctorate journey.

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.section: Taking a Chance to Change Her Life and Others
chunks.text: Isler arrived from Turkey with two suitcases and a hotel reservation near UCF.

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.section: Taking a Chance to Change Her Life and Others
chunks.text: “My mom filled one of the suitcases with Turkish food,” Isler says. She can laugh now, but at the time, she had no clear path beyond the airport. “I had to figure everything out.”

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.section: Taking a Chance to Change Her Life and Others
chunks.text: A few years earlier, she traveled across the globe to UCF as an undergraduate, having earned a competitive internship in the Synthetic Reality Lab, where she worked with Pegasus Professor Charles Hughes and then computer engineering doctoral student Kamran Ali '21PhD on facial expression recognition.

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.section: Taking a Chance to Change Her Life and Others
chunks.text: “She committed herself to the research,” Hughes says, “and even contributed to writing and editing the resulting report after she returned to Turkey.”

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.section: Taking a Chance to Change Her Life and Others
chunks.text: Days away from starting doctorate-level research, with all her belongings in a single piece of luggage, Isler would do what she does best: find a way. She moved from the hotel to an unfurnished apartment.

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.section: Taking a Chance to Change Her Life and Others
chunks.text: But with her, Isler brought two specific interests to her postgraduate research at UCF. Her mother, a dentist in Turkey, inspired an interest in medical advancement. Her father, a computer science professor, recognized in his daughter the curiosity and determination required for the field.

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.section: Taking a Chance to Change Her Life and Others
chunks.text: “If I know an idea can be impactful, I'll do whatever is necessary to make it a reality,” she says. “The higher the stakes, the more driven I become.”

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.section: Taking a Chance to Change Her Life and Others
chunks.text: Those stakes led her to focus on medical imaging solutions for cancer care worldwide. Without a medical background, she collaborated with doctors. It helped that she never looked at her research as an academic exercise. She wanted only to deliver something trustworthy that clinicians everywhere could use to eliminate gray areas in image analysis.

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.section: Taking a Chance to Change Her Life and Others
chunks.text: “I've been fortunate to work with many doctoral students over the years, and Ilkin stands out on multiple levels,” says Mohaisen, pointing out her motivation, energy and curiosity, before adding: “I'd say she is among the most driven.”

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.text: By now, the source of Isler's uncommon drive is clear. Every time someone showed skepticism about her powerlifting, she responded by breaking a national record. Although she could have attended a private college in Turkey, where she would have been surrounded by familiar language and culture, she instead chose to move across the world to study AI.

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.text: There's one more motivation that consistently guides her: others.

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.text: Isler considers her greatest accomplishment in powerlifting to be the doors she helped open for others in Turkey to try any form of fitness they choose. And she says she would gladly move to another continent again, with just a suitcase and her AI skills, if it meant helping improve the lives of others.

chunks.source_title: The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News)
chunks.text: “When I look back, I can see that I've often traded comfort for growth,” she says, “and I will not hesitate to do it again.”
I moved from Turkey to the United States to pursue AI at UCF, where I earned my MS in Computer Science in 2022 and my PhD in 2025.

At work I build enterprise AI systems: an in-house AI platform for deploying, orchestrating, and governing AI tools, agents, and multi-agent workflows (including MCP servers, tool calling, and agent skills), LLM evaluation and hallucination detection pipelines, and human-in-the-loop tools for finance and cost estimating. On my own time I build personal AI assistants for home workflows and daily automation, and this site's grounded assistant.

One of my two main initiatives at work is AI for finance reporting and forecasting. Finance teams kept a separate, frequently reworked spreadsheet for every project, so monthly reporting meant hours of manual consolidation. As solution architect, I designed from scratch, and led the developers who built, human-in-the-loop AI tools that bring project finance data into one adaptable source of truth, surface the top cost drivers each month, flag transactions worth a closer look, and support forecasting while the analyst stays in control of every number. I started from how analysts actually close a month, kept every output reviewable, and evaluated new methods before they reached the team. Cash Flow & Earned Value is in production with 70+ finance users globally, saving 15–30 minutes per analysis and about an hour per forecast; Monthly Update Insights and Risk & Contingency have their first versions in production, with more in development.

My other main initiative is AI-assisted cost estimating, which I lead along with its developers. Estimating large, one-of-a-kind projects depends on deep expertise and messy, non-standardized inputs, and the estimators were skeptical at first. I designed from scratch, and my developers built, the Estimator Builder: a suite of 12 purpose-built, human-in-the-loop applications for about 80 users, with 6+ shipped, that read design drawings to draft scope, turn messy scope lists into structured estimates and track how they change, and retrieve everything previously paid for an item. Instead of replacing their Excel workflows, the tools accept their existing files and return results in the same format; we started with small validated wins and added automation as trust grew. The conversation moved from whether it would work to what else we could automate. I am also building, from scratch and as the sole engineer (Python and Neo4j, deployed through our CI/CD pipeline), a project-intelligence tool on a temporal knowledge-graph architecture similar to Graphiti: project decks, schedules, and budget updates are ingested as episodes, an LLM extracts entities and relationships into a graph, facts keep their history instead of being overwritten, and retrieval combines semantic search, keyword search, and graph traversal. It gives senior leadership one view of what changed across a project and how it affects budgets, plans, and schedules.

My research is about building AI that people can rely on, which starts with knowing when a model is wrong. During my PhD I designed 3D neural network architectures, loss functions, and uncertainty quantification methods for tumor and organ-at-risk segmentation; my self-supervised and uncertainty-guided approaches achieved state-of-the-art results at publication. Today I apply the same idea to LLMs: retrieval-augmented generation, hallucination detection, groundedness and citation checks, and evaluation pipelines that decide when an answer can be trusted, or when the system should decline to answer.

Selected publications with links: Pancreas CT/MRI segmentation (2025) https://doi.org/10.1016/j.media.2024.103382; Power-VR (2022) https://doi.org/10.1002/cav.2045; Uncertainty-Guided Tumor Segmentation (2025) https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2504.12215; OAR and Tumor Segmentation with UQ (2023) https://doi.org/10.1109/ICECCME57830.2023.10252269; Enhancing OAR Segmentation (2022) https://doi.org/10.1117/12.2611498; Facial Expression Translation (2019) https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1910.05595; Generative AI in Medical Imaging (2024) https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-72787-0_17. Full list: https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=ZgPdlJ0AAAAJ&hl=en.

My powerlifting PRs are Squat 355 lbs, Bench 200 lbs, and Deadlift 475 lbs. I am a European powerlifting champion (1st Place Overall at the IPSU European Championship) and a two-time Overall Champion of Türkiye. I am still holding deadlift records in Turkiye since 2020 and in Florida since 2022. These include both junior and open records, and I broke both while I was a junior. Sources: USAPL records database https://usapl.liftingdatabase.com/records-default?priority=0&recordtypeid=120382&categoryid=&weightclassid= and IPF Turkiye records https://powerlifting.org.tr/turkiye-rekorlari.
My featured story is The Mind to Move Mountains (UCF News): https://www.ucf.edu/news/the-mind-to-move-mountains/.

You can reach me at ilkinisler@gmail.com. LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/ilkinsevgiisler/. Google Scholar: https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=ZgPdlJ0AAAAJ&hl=en. GitHub: https://github.com/ilkinisler.

This assistant answers only from my resume, the UCF News feature, and these first-party facts. It uses hybrid retrieval (BM25-style keyword matching plus embedding similarity), declines to answer when retrieval confidence is low instead of guessing, and checks that each answer sentence is supported by a source. I built it as a small, public example of the grounded, hallucination-aware systems I build at work.
